sections.h2: Which West Virginia laws cover landlords and tenants?
sections.html:
Three parts of the West Virginia Code do most of the work: Chapter 37, Article 6 (landlord and tenant), Chapter 37, Article 6A (residential rental security deposits) and Chapter 55, Article 3A (remedies for wrongful occupation of residential rental property). Together they cover repairs, deposits, notice to end a tenancy and the court route for removing a tenant.

If you own a rental you are thinking of selling, these are the rules the buyer inherits. They also decide how fast a tenant can be moved out if the sale needs an empty house.

  • Article 6 lists 31 sections, from transfer of the landlord's interest (37-6-1) to the habitability duty (37-6-30).
  • Article 6A has six sections: definitions, deposits, records, prohibited lease terms, landlord noncompliance and effective date.
  • Article 3A has three sections: the petition, defenses and the court proceeding.

sections.h2: What happens to a tenant's lease when the landlord sells the rental?
sections.html:
The lease does not disappear. Under W. Va. Code 37-6-1, a grantee or assignee of leased land, or of the reversion, can use the same conditions, forfeitures and lease covenants the original lessor could have used. Section 37-6-2 gives the tenant the matching benefit: a lessee may enforce the lease's conditions, covenants and promises against whoever takes the reversion, as if that person were the original lessor, except for warranties.

For a seller, that means a signed lease is part of what you are selling. A buyer takes the property subject to the tenant's rights, and the tenant can hold the new owner to the lease terms.

The deposit follows the property too. Section 37-6A-2(e) says whoever holds the landlord's interest when the tenancy ends is bound by the deposit rules and must return any deposit that is duly owed to the tenant. That applies whether or not the deposit was handed over in the sale and regardless of any contract between the old and new landlord. If you sell a rental with a tenant in place, settle in writing who is carrying the deposit, because the tenant can look to the new owner.

sections.h2: How do security deposits work in West Virginia?
sections.html:
At the end of the tenancy and within the applicable notice period, the landlord must deliver the deposit, minus deductions, together with a written itemization (37-6A-2(a)). The statute limits what the landlord may deduct.

Allowed uses of the deposit under 37-6A-2(b):

  • Rent due, including reasonable late charges stated in the rental agreement.
  • Damages from the tenant's noncompliance with the rental agreement, less reasonable wear and tear.
  • Unpaid utilities that the landlord billed, paid and that the tenant owed under the agreement.
  • Reasonable costs to remove and store the tenant's personal property.
  • Other charges in the rental agreement, including a third-party contractor's repair of tenant damage.

When damages exceed the deposit and need an outside contractor, the landlord must give written notice within the notice period and then has an extra fifteen days to send the itemization and repair cost (37-6A-2(c)). Delivery can be personal or by mail to the last known or forwarding address. If a mailed deposit comes back undeliverable, the landlord holds it for six months and must hand it over within 72 hours of a written request (37-6A-2(g)).

sections.h2: What does a landlord owe in return for a tenant's rent?
sections.html:
West Virginia requires a landlord of residential property to deliver the unit fit and habitable and to keep it that way (W. Va. Code 37-6-30(a)(1)). The same subsection spells out the duties.

  • Meet applicable health, safety, fire and housing codes, unless the tenant, a family member or a guest caused the failure.
  • Keep common areas of multiple housing units clean, safe and in repair.
  • Make repairs needed to keep the premises fit, except those caused mainly by the tenant's lack of reasonable care.
  • Keep electrical, plumbing, sanitary, heating, ventilating and air-conditioning facilities in safe working order when the landlord supplies them.
  • In multiple units, provide for removal of garbage and waste.
  • Where units have direct public utility connections, supply running water, reasonable hot water, and reasonable heat from October 1 through the last day of April.

Two limits matter. A greater duty written into the rental agreement controls over the statute (37-6-30(b)). And the section does not require the landlord to make repairs while the tenant is in arrears on rent (37-6-30(c)). For an owner selling a rental, deferred repairs on a unit with a tenant in place can become a dispute, which is one reason some owners prefer a buyer who takes the property as it stands.

sections.h2: How does a landlord remove a tenant through the courts?
sections.html:
The landlord files a verified petition in magistrate court or circuit court in the county where the property sits (W. Va. Code 55-3A-1). The sheriff removes a tenant who stays past the date set in the court's order (55-3A-3(f)).

StepWhat the statute says
PetitionOwner or agent states the right to possession, describes the property and alleges rent arrears, breach of a warranty or lease covenant, or deliberate or negligent damage (55-3A-1(a))
Hearing dateCourt sets a hearing not less than five nor more than 10 judicial days after filing (55-3A-1(b))
NoticeServed under Rule 4 of the Rules of Civil Procedure or by certified mail, return receipt requested; tenant may file a written defense within five days of receiving it (55-3A-1(c))
No responseIf the tenant files nothing by the hearing, the court enters an order granting immediate possession (55-3A-3(a))
ContestedIf the tenant answers, the court holds a hearing; continuances are for cause only, and a tenant who gets one must pay periodic rent into court (55-3A-3(d))
OrderCourt sets the vacate time; if the tenant stays, the sheriff removes the tenant (55-3A-3(f))

A tenant may raise any defense available in an ejectment or unlawful detainer action (55-3A-2). In a rent case, a tenant who answers that the landlord breached a material covenant on which the duty to pay rent depends gets a hearing on that issue (55-3A-3(b)).

sections.h2: What can a landlord do with belongings left behind?
sections.html:
After a possession order, the landlord can dispose of property the tenant says in writing is abandoned, or of garbage, without liability (55-3A-3(h)(1)). Otherwise the landlord may remove and store the items, or leave them in place, and may dispose of them after thirty days if the tenant has not paid the reasonable costs and has not reclaimed them, or if storage costs equal the value of the goods.

If the property is worth more than $300 and the tenant or a secured party says they intend to collect it, the landlord must store it up to thirty more days, provided they pay reasonable storage and removal costs (55-3A-3(i)).

A different process applies when the tenant has simply left. Under 37-6-6, if a tenant who owes rent abandons the property, the landlord posts a written notice in a conspicuous place requiring payment within one month. If the rent is unpaid, the landlord gets possession and the tenant's right ends. Before disposing of belongings the landlord must post and mail a notice by first-class mail with a certificate of mailing, giving a removal date at least thirty days after mailing (sixty days if the tenant is on active military duty and has said so).

sections.h2: What can a tenant do if the landlord keeps the deposit?
sections.html:
If a landlord's noncompliance with Article 6A is willful or not in good faith, the tenant is entitled to a judgment for the unreturned deposit plus damages for annoyance or inconvenience equal to one and a half times the amount wrongfully withheld (37-6A-5(a)). When the tenant owes rent, the court credits that award against the rent due.

Civil actions under the article go to magistrate court or circuit court in the county where the rental sits (37-6A-5(b)).

sections.h2: How do these rules affect selling a rental house in West Virginia?
sections.html:
They set the clock and the cost. A sale with a tenant in place carries the lease, the deposit and the repair duty to the buyer. A sale that needs vacant possession means going through the 55-3A court process first, and that depends on a valid ground such as unpaid rent or damage.

Owners who sell to us for cash can choose either route. We buy houses as-is, including rentals with tenants, and the offer is written for the situation you describe. Before you sign anything, check your lease, your deposit records and any notices you have served. Get advice from a West Virginia attorney or Legal Aid of West Virginia's renters' rights pages if a dispute is open. This page is general information, not legal advice.

faqs.q: Does a West Virginia tenant have to move out when the landlord sells the house?
faqs.a: No, not by reason of the sale alone. Under W. Va. Code 37-6-1 and 37-6-2, the buyer of the landlord's interest takes it subject to the lease, and the tenant can enforce the lease terms against the new owner. Ending the tenancy still follows the lease and the notice rules.

faqs.q: How long does a West Virginia landlord have to return a security deposit?
faqs.a: The deposit, minus lawful deductions and with a written itemization, is due on termination and within the applicable notice period (37-6A-2(a)). If damages exceed the deposit and need a contractor, the landlord gets an extra fifteen days after giving written notice to itemize the cost.

faqs.q: Can a landlord cut off heat or lock a tenant out in West Virginia?
faqs.a: The statutes we reviewed provide a court process for removal (55-3A), with the sheriff enforcing a possession order. Section 37-6-30 also requires reasonable heat from October 1 through April 30 where the landlord supplies it through a direct utility connection. Ask a West Virginia attorney about any specific lockout.

faqs.q: What is the penalty if a landlord wrongfully withholds a deposit?
faqs.a: If the noncompliance is willful or not in good faith, the tenant can recover the unreturned deposit plus damages of one and a half times the amount wrongfully withheld (37-6A-5(a)).

faqs.q: Can I sell a rental house with a tenant still living in it?
faqs.a: Yes. The lease and the deposit obligation travel with the property, so the buyer steps into the landlord's position. A cash buyer who purchases as-is can take a tenant-occupied house, and you can raise that when you ask for an offer.
